numberItems.stem: How long must the shipper keep shipping papers for hazardous waste?
numberItems.explanation: The shipper keeps hazardous waste papers for 3 years; other HazMat papers are kept 2 years (p. 9-8).

numberItems.stem: Where must placards go on a placarded vehicle?
options: Front and rear only, at least 2
Both sides and both ends, at least 4 identical
numberItems.explanation: Placards go on both sides and both ends: at least 4 identical placards, readable from all 4 directions (pp. 9-5, 9-9).

numberItems.stem: How many rules does the handbook list for how each placard must be mounted and kept?
numberItems.explanation: There are 6: easily seen, level and left to right, at least 3 inches from other markings, clear of attachments, clean and undamaged, on a contrasting background (p. 9-9).

numberItems.stem: How many facts do you need to decide which placards (if any) to use?
numberItems.explanation: You need 3 facts: the hazard class, the amount of HazMat shipped, and the total weight of all HazMat classes on your vehicle (p. 9-9).

numberItems.stem: How many placard tables are there?
numberItems.explanation: There are 2 placard tables: Table 1 (placard any amount) and Table 2 (placard at 1,001 lb or more) (p. 9-10).

numberItems.stem: Table 2 materials in non-bulk packages need placards when the total reaches:
options: 1,001 lb or more, including the packages
2,205 lb or more of each class
numberItems.explanation: Table 2 needs placards at 1,001 lb or more, counting the packages and adding all shipping papers (p. 9-10).

numberItems.stem: When may you use DANGEROUS placards?
options: Whenever you carry any Table 1 material
Only when one Table 2 class reaches 2,205 lb
For 2 or more Table 2 classes needing different placards, totaling 1,001 lb or more
numberItems.explanation: DANGEROUS placards are an option for 1,001 lb or more of 2 or more Table 2 classes that need different placards (p. 9-10).

numberItems.stem: You may NOT cover a Table 2 class with a DANGEROUS placard if you loaded how much of it at one place?
numberItems.explanation: If 2,205 lb or more of one Table 2 class was loaded at one place, use that material's specific placard (p. 9-10).

numberItems.stem: Which Class 7 radioactive materials are in Placard Table 1 (placard any amount)?
options: Those with a Yellow III label only
Radioactive material in bulk packaging only
numberItems.explanation: Table 1 lists Class 7 radioactive with a Yellow III label only (p. 9-10).

numberItems.stem: Which Division 6.1 poisons are in Placard Table 1 (placard any amount)?
options: Inhalation hazard zone A and B only
numberItems.explanation: Table 1 covers 6.1 inhalation hazard zone A and B only; other 6.1 poisons are in Table 2 (p. 9-10).

numberItems.stem: Which of these has NO placard?
numberItems.explanation: Placard Table 2 lists no placard for 6.2 infectious substances and ORM-D (p. 9-10).

numberItems.stem: Most bulk packages must be placarded on how many sides?
numberItems.explanation: Most bulk packages are placarded on all 4 sides; only certain ones may use 2 opposite sides or labels (p. 9-11).
